target: Var hon bor är en hemlighet med familjen.
english: Where she lives is a secret with the family.
tip: Indirect question as subject: "Var hon bor" = where she lives.

target: Vad vacker hon var på stationen varje morgon!
english: How beautiful she was at the station every morning!
tip: Exclamatory word order: "Vad" + adjective + subject + verb.

target: Min familj bor i en liten stad i södern.
english: My family lives in a small town in the south.
tip: Liten is irregular: you say en liten stad, but the plural is små, which looks nothing like liten.

target: Skynda dig så att vi inte missar bussen dit!
english: Hurry up so we don't miss the bus!
tip: In a subordinate clause inte comes before the verb: så att vi inte missar. Compare the main-clause order verb before inte.

target: Han brände maten och vi fick beställa pizza istället.
english: He burned the food and we had to order pizza instead.
tip: fick, the past of få, often means 'had to': vi fick beställa pizza = we had to order pizza.

target: Vi lagade en stor middag med tre rätter i fredags.
english: We cooked a large dinner with three courses last Friday.
tip: i plus a weekday plus -s means 'last': i fredags = last Friday.

target: Jag ringde min syster och vi pratade i en timme.
english: I called my sister and we talked for an hour.
tip: i marks a duration you spent: pratade i en timme = talked for an hour.

target: Hon åt en stor lunch och drack kaffe på restaurangen.
english: She ate a large lunch and drank coffee at the restaurant.
tip: Strong verbs change their vowel in the past: dricka becomes drack = drank.

target: När hon fick reda på vad som hänt såg hon rött och slog igen dörren.
english: When she found out what had happened, she saw red and slammed the door.
tip: få reda på means to find out: fick reda på vad som hänt.

target: Han viskade att han hade en hemlighet.
english: He whispered that he had a secret.
tip: Unlike English 'that,' att is normally kept in reported speech: viskade att han hade en hemlighet.

target: Dykaren utforskade det sjunkna skeppet på havsbotten.
english: The diver explored the sunken ship on the seabed.
tip: Participles work as adjectives and take -a when definite: det sjunkna skeppet = the sunken ship.

target: Snart kommer sommaren under sommaren till slut.
english: Soon summer will come during the summer in the end.
tip: A fronted adverb pushes the verb ahead of the subject: Snart kommer sommaren, not Snart sommaren kommer.

english: No, thank you.
tip: tack means both please and thank you: nej tack declines an offer, ja tack accepts it.

english: I don't know.
tip: Swedish splits know: vet (from veta) is knowing a fact, as in jag vet inte. Knowing a person uses känner.

english: Talk to you soon.
tip: The -s ending can mean each other: hörs, from höra (hear), is a set phrase for we will be in touch.

english: It is three o'clock.
tip: To tell time say Klockan är plus the number: Klockan är tre, literally the clock is three, for it is three o'clock.

english: She speaks Swedish well.
tip: Language names stay lowercase in Swedish: svenska, not Svenska, even elsewhere in a sentence.

english: That can't be right.
tip: In a main clause inte follows the verb: Det kan inte stämma. Putting inte first is wrong.

english: Seventy, eighty, ninety, a hundred.
tip: The tens end in -tio, from tio (ten): sjuttio (70), åttio (80), nittio (90).

english: Six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
tip: Sju (seven) starts with the sj-sound written [ɧ], the hardest sound in Swedish, made deep in the throat.

english: Eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen.
tip: Teens 13 to 19 add -ton to the base digit: tretton (13), fjorton (14), femton (15).

english: Sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, twenty.
tip: sjutton (17) doubles as a mild exclamation like darn in sjutton också, besides just meaning seventeen.

english: It is ten to twelve.
tip: For minutes before the hour use i (to): tio i tolv means ten to twelve. i points ahead to the next hour.

english: It is five past eight.
tip: For minutes after the hour use över (past): fem över åtta means five past eight.

english: She wondered where we lived.
tip: A reported wh-question keeps the subject before the verb: var vi bodde, not var bodde vi.

english: I am twenty-five years old.
tip: State age with vara plus år gammal: jag är tjugofem år gammal. In everyday speech gammal is often dropped.

english: The big car is mine.
tip: Definite adjective phrases double the marking: den stora bilen has den, the -a on stora, and the -en ending on bilen.

english: The soup is warm and good.
tip: After är, adjectives match the noun. Soppan is an en-word, so varm and god take no ending.

english: We took them to the hotel.
tip: dem is the object form of de (they): vi förde dem till hotellet.

target: Vi flyttar till en ny stad.
english: We are moving to a new city.
tip: Swedish has no -ing form: flyttar covers both we move and we are moving. Present tense does the job.
